source.title: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Yi-Zheng Yang; Hai-Ning Yu; Yue-Chen Wang; Yi-Kai Hou; Xing Fu; Jin-Bo Yang; Tian-Qing Zhu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether refusal-related directions and their onset behavior affect safety in reasoning models, but uses its own vector extraction and first-token interventions rather than the original difference-in-means, all-layer ablation method.
record.gate_note: Reports measurements of refusal-vector projections and outcomes from steering or injecting the vectors. The prefix-only interventions and SafeToken results are not rows because they do not apply the refusal direction itself. The table’s direction-steering results and the direction-injection results are included; SafeToken’s separate learned embedding is not.
record.test_reason: The study extracts layer-wise refusal vectors from instruction-tuned models, using safety-head ablation rather than difference-in-means. It then steers same-family distilled reasoning models with them in both directions, and injects them at the first generated token, reporting attack success rates (Tables 1, 3). This is a different method aimed at whether a linear refusal direction causally controls refusal, applied to transferred vectors in reasoning models.
record.authors_conclusion:
Largely correct. Two additions:
- the authors claim that refusal vectors from instruction-tuned models transfer to same-backbone reasoning models (Table 1);
- they claim that ORC at the first token makes an important causal contribution to unsafe outputs.
They also attribute SafeToken's weaker jailbreak robustness to attacks that disrupt harmfulness recognition before onset.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives layer-wise refusal vectors using safety-head ablation contributions and uses projection analysis and first-token injection/steering. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction or ablate it across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured onset effect differs across matched model pairs; the paper also reports that injection position matters for its separate SafeToken method, not for the refusal-direction intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Onset Refusal Collapse. Projection onto the transferred refusal direction tracks the instruction-tuned model during prompt encoding, then drops sharply at the first generated token in the reasoning models. RORC is 189% for the Llama pair, 20% for Qwen-7B and 100% for Qwen-14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models, the refusal-direction signal is present over the prompt but collapses at generation onset, and how much it collapses varies by model pair.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-token attribution for the first-token Okay/Sorry margin. Compared with the instruction-tuned model, the reasoning model ranks harmful tokens earlier but shows stronger dominance of structural tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning models' affirmative onset token is driven by instruction and structural tokens rather than harmful content (attribution evidence, opposite objectives).

record.problems: The direction-steering table does not state steering strengths or uncertainty. Direction interventions are evaluated on harmful-query safety measures only, with no general-capability evaluation or harmless-request refusal test. The token-attribution evidence is not a direct measure of a separately encoded harmfulness judgment.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Not tested: transfer across languages, from base to instruct, or across unrelated families. Only same-family instruction-tuned to distilled-reasoning transfer is tested, on R1-7B and R1-8B.
Not tested. The authors only speculate that jailbreaks alter harmfulness recognition; there is no test of direction suppression.
Not tested: per-layer vectors are used, but multi-dimensionality is never examined.
Not tested. Only input-token attribution is reported; no separate harmfulness representation is probed or intervened on.

missing.what: Prefix-only control for direction injection. Force-decoded safety prefixes of 1–8 tokens give StrongReject ASR of 15.65–27.80 for R1-7B and 3.51–10.54 for R1-8B, comparable to or better than refusal-direction injection. A researcher needs this to judge how specific the direction's effect is.

record.verdict_notes: The direction is obtained by ablating 200 EAP-IG-selected safety heads and fitting per-layer vectors (Algorithm 1), not by difference-in-means. No intervention reports harmless-prompt refusal or utility; SafeToken's utility results do not apply to the direction interventions. r10-r13 and r14-r17 record the same Table 9 comparisons twice. In Table 3, R1-8B injection (7.35) equals the prefix-length-5 value, which may be a coincidence or a table error.

versions.untested_parts: Does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction; does not ablate it at every layer and position, test refusal of harmless requests after addition, or evaluate general capability under the direction intervention.

Does not directly test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded representations; uses input-token attribution to contrast harmful-content and structural-token contributions.
Tests transfer from instruction-tuned models to reasoning models in the same model families; does not test languages or transfer across unrelated families.
Tests three distilled reasoning models, not reasoning models generally; does not test the original all-layer ablation or addition procedure.

rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized onset change in the matched instruction-tuned/reasoning-model refusal-projection gap
rows.note: The paper defines positive RORC as a widening of the refusal-projection gap at generation onset.
rows.check: RORC is a normalized change in the instruction-tuned vs reasoning-model gap in projection onto the refusal direction at generation onset. It is a projection statistic, not a rate of refusal or a causal test of the direction, so it does not measure what V1, V6 or V8 name. It belongs under fits_no_version (the Onset Refusal Collapse finding).

relationships.condition: Safety-head-derived refusal vectors steered or injected in R1-7B and R1-8B, measured by harmful-benchmark ASR
relationships.reason: The causal effect runs in both predicted directions but is incomplete at the reported settings. Negative steering leaves 13–25% of harmful prompts refused (ASR 75%/87%); positive steering and onset injection leave 7–27% ASR (r1-r4, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Negative steering left 13–25% of harmful prompts refused at ASR 75% and 87%, while positive steering and onset injection left ASR at 7–27%.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Safety-head-derived refusal vectors steered or injected in R1-7B and R1-8B, measured by harmful-benchmark ASR
source_check.reason: All the linked rows use a vector that is not difference-in-means, transferred from another model, in distilled reasoning models only, at unstated strengths. That is the setting of V6 and V8, not V1, and V8 already carries the same incompleteness. There is no own-model steering or ablation in a chat model, and the partial effect cannot be separated from transfer or strength choice. If the catalog does link reasoning-model rows to V1, limits_scope is the mechanical label, but it double-counts V8.

relationships.display_finding: Transferred vectors moved ASR from 45% to 21% or 75% and from 59% to 27% or 87%, while first-token injection lowered StrongReject ASR.

relation.reason: Table 1 tests two-sided steering with the vectors, and Table 3 tests direction injection against ASR. Both are the study's own causal results on the direction.

tranche.reason: The refusal vector is extracted differently (safety-head ablation, not difference-in-means). The study reports causal steering and injection results on ASR (Tables 1 and 3), so it tests the claim and does not just use the vector as a tool.

source_check.notes: The refusal vectors are not harmful-minus-harmless means. Each layer's vector is the mean residual change from ablating 200 EAP-IG safety heads in the IT model on harmful prompts (Alg. 1). Table 1 gives no strength, layers, judge, n or CIs, and the record's uncertainty=y rests only on Table 2's bootstrap CIs for the ORC statistic. The authors_conclusion paraphrase matches the text.

statements.correction: The vectors are one per layer. Each is the mean residual change from ablating 200 EAP-IG safety heads in the IT model on harmful prompts (Alg. 1), not harmful minus harmless means. Table 1 does not state steering layers or strength. Injection is at every layer, at the first generated token only, with per-layer strength from an MLP probe (App. E.2). Tables 1 and 3 have no CIs; bootstrap CIs are given only for the Table 2 ORC statistic. There is no random-direction control.
statements.problem: The numbers for this study are right, but the conditions are wrong for it. 'A selected layer and strength' does not describe it, and the wording implies a difference-in-means direction. The 'why' credits it with uncertainty that the cited tables lack.

statements.correction: r8: R1-7B StrongReject ASR 49.20->15.02. r9: R1-8B 37.38->7.35, with refusal-direction injection at the first generated token. The study's relevant finding is ORC: during the prompt, the LRM's refusal projection tracks the IT model's, then drops sharply at the first generated token (Fig. 2). Table 2 gives mean R_ORC 189.41% (Llama-8B), 20.00% (Qwen-7B) and 100.11% (Qwen-14B), n=100 each.
statements.problem: The item cites r8 and r9 but says nothing about this study. Those rows show that first-token injection works; they do not show the reasoning path limiting where the direction acts.

statements.correction: The vectors come from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via safety-head ablation (Alg. 1) and are applied to R1-8B and R1-7B. Table 1 gives no judge, n or uncertainty.
statements.problem: The numbers and 'strengths not stated' are right. The item omits that the vectors are safety-head-derived and transferred from the IT counterpart, which confounds 'partial'.
